explanations.Paul Ricard: The French racing circuit at Le Castellet, inland from Marseille.
explanations.Silverstone: The English circuit that is the long-standing home of the British Grand Prix.
explanations.Monza: The fast Italian race track just north of Milan.
explanations.Paris Marathon: The marathon run each spring through the streets of Paris.
explanations.London Marathon: The marathon run each year from Blackheath to The Mall in London.
explanations.Rome Marathon: The marathon hosted every year by the city of Rome.
explanations.Tour de France: The three-week cycling race held mainly on French roads.
explanations.Tour of Britain: The stage race for cyclists held on British roads.
explanations.Giro d'Italia: The long stage race for cyclists held mainly in Italy.

sources.excerpt: The Circuit Paul Ricard (French pronunciation: [siʁkɥi pɔl ʁikaʁ]) is a French motorsport race track built in 1969 at Le Castellet, Var, near Marseille, with finance from pastis magnate Paul Ricard.
The 1950 British Grand Prix at Silverstone was the first race in the newly created World Championship of Drivers.
The Monza Circuit, officially called the Autodromo Nazionale Monza (Italian for 'Monza National Autodrome'), is a 5.793 km (3.600 mi) race track near the city of Monza, north of Milan, in Italy.
The Paris Marathon (French: Marathon de Paris) is an annual marathon hosted by the city of Paris, France.
The London Marathon is an annual marathon held in London, England.
The Rome Marathon (Italian: Maratona di Roma) is an annual marathon competition hosted by the city of Rome, Italy.
The Tour de France (pronounced [tuʁ də fʁɑ̃s]; lit. 'Tour of France') is an annual men's multiple-stage road cycling race held primarily in France.
The Tour of Britain is a multi-stage cycling race, conducted on British roads, in which participants race across Great Britain to complete the race in the fastest time.
The Giro d'Italia (pronounced [ˈdʒiːro diˈtaːlja]; lit. 'Tour of Italy'), also known simply as the Giro, is an annual multiple-stage road cycling race primarily held in Italy.

editorNotes: Each tile is an event or a place, and all nine belong to one sport and one country, so every tile fits a single cell and the grid can be read only one way. The pairs worth checking are the cycling ones. The Tour de France has begun in Britain more than once, in London in 2007 and in Yorkshire in 2014, but it is a French race that is run almost entirely in France, so it is not offered the British cell that the Tour of Britain takes. The Giro d'Italia has also started abroad, yet it is held primarily in Italy. Paul Ricard, Silverstone and Monza are motor racing circuits and not road courses for cycling or running, and the three marathons are named for the cities that hold them, so none of them can move between columns. Giro d'Italia keeps its apostrophe because that is the spelling every source uses.
